cards.title: POST /ingest — versioned
items: Version = hash of text, metadata, chunking and embedding model; chunk ids are {doc}:{version}:{i}
Under a per-document lock: embed all chunks, upsert them into Chroma, then flip the pointer with one SQLite transaction (INSERT OR REPLACE into document_versions)
Older chunks are deleted after the flip; a failure before it keeps the previous version active
Re-ingesting identical content is a no-op

cards.title: POST /query — hybrid
items: One snapshot of active versions filters both searches, so readers never see a mix of versions
Vector ranking from Chroma (cosine) and BM25 ranking over active chunks, each top 4·k
Fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion: score = Σ 1 / (60 + rank)

cards.title: State split
items: ChromaDB holds only the chunk collection: text, vectors and _version metadata
SQLite system.db (stdlib sqlite3, beside Chroma's files in CHROMA_PATH) holds the active-version pointers and the embedding-model stamp
Keeping pointers out of a second Chroma collection removed chromadb 1.5.9's vector loss: 0 of 2,000 stress sequences lost data

cards.title: POST /conversations
items: RoundRobin picks the next agent; rotation restarts on every run
RAG query uses the task on turn 1, then the latest reply
Retrieved chunks travel in a separate user message inside <documents>; the system prompt only adds a rule to treat them as untrusted data
Stops at max_turns (at most 20) or when a reply contains stop_token
LLMClient also supports response_format (JSON Schema, validated); the conversation loop does not use it

cards.title: Guardrails
items: Strict Pydantic models with size caps: document 50k chars, query 1k, task 4k, ≤ 8 agents, system prompt 4k, stop_token 64
Raw body over 1 MB → 413 before parsing; Host header must be in ALLOWED_HOSTS; docs off when ENV=production
Ollama unreachable or erroring → 503, timeout → 504, with fixed messages and no exception text
At startup the embedding model and dimension recorded in system.db must match the embedder
Chroma anonymized telemetry is disabled on the persistent client

cards.title: Observability
items: Loguru writes one JSON object per line to stderr
Every log of a conversation carries its conversation_id, including retrieval logs
Task, reply and document text are never logged
Uvicorn access logs are still plain text

cards.title: Planned — not implemented
